title: What If You Stood on the Surface of Venus?

scenes.text: What if you stood on Venus? The longest any machine has lasted there is shorter than a movie.
First the air: about ninety six percent carbon dioxide, with high clouds made of sulfuric acid droplets.
At the surface it is about four hundred sixty degrees Celsius, hot enough to melt lead.
The pressure is about ninety times sea level on Earth, enough to crush an unprotected probe quickly.
In nineteen seventy, Venera Seven became the first craft to send data back from another planet's surface.
The record is Venera Thirteen in nineteen eighty two: one hundred twenty seven minutes, about four times its planned lifetime.

description:
What if you stood on the surface of Venus?
About 460 C, about 90 times Earth's pressure, and sulfuric acid clouds. The best probe ever, Venera 13, survived 127 minutes.
